title: Clarinet, bass and piano players with Dimes; early pianists
summary: He names the clarinetist (Blind Freddy), the bassist T-Boy, and talks about pianists such as Victor Viall, Tony Jackson and Buddy Christian.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Who was the clarinet with Wesley Dimes? How was he? No, clarinet. Who was the clarinet player with Wesley Dimes?

Well, we just had one kind of player. So who was he? Who was the clarinet player? Oh, uh, Blind Freddy. Blind Freddy. Yeah. I see. Blind Freddy was a clarinet player at that time. Bass? T-boy. He called him Eddie Gilmore. He called him T-boy. He worked out by T-boy. Let's see. Now uh... Fetty Boo Boo. Yeah, Thumbo. You know, we called him Fetty Boo Boo, but he was...
We ain't no piano player then.

Now he doesn't ever get a job. We were high piano players. We had to see a father sometime, uh... We called him Professor. Victor Viall. You ever heard him? No, I don't know. He's a sissy father, you know. He's good. You remember him, Victor Viall. He could play with Franky Duce and all of them, you know. But when we get a piano, you didn't hear some of the piano players coming up. No. No. Most of them was good. Yeah. Funny fellas, huh? Funny fellas, huh? Funny fellas, huh? Funny fellas, huh? Funny fellas, huh? Funny fellas, huh?

Yeah. Says the piano player was funny fellas, huh? Yeah. Yeah. Most of them like Tony Jackson and all of them, you know, like that. And I forget, there was about five or six of them, you know.
